rows.grounds: Direct object describing the essence to be heard; lexical hint: nectar.
Compound denoting the true nature of Kaula; object in apposition to amṛtaṃ.
Imperative command addressed to the listener.
Compound adjective qualifying kaulasadbhāvaṃ as consisting of kāmakalā.

items.question: What essential nature characterizes the nectar-like Kaula reality to be heard?
premises: The Kaula true nature is described as nectar.
This Kaula reality is to be heard.
items.inference: The nectar-like Kaula true nature that is to be heard is essentially constituted by kāmakalā.
uncertainties: The precise doctrinal sense of kāmakalā in this context is not fully specified by the verse alone.
items.plain_english: Hear of the nectar, the true nature of Kaula, whose essence is kāmakalā.
